key_highlights: ASX rose on the session as oil prices and bond yields eased, with big four banks (CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX) advancing; RBA chief flagged inflation concerns ahead of the next rate decision
RBA leaders warned rates are only just back to a 'sensible level', signalling no near-term cuts; IMF separately urged fiscal consolidation as another hike looms
Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure threaten a Middle East oil shock, pressuring energy costs and global risk sentiment
Japan hiked rates to counter 'shocking' inflation, adding pressure on AUD/USD and Australian bond markets
Recession odds for 2027 have increased; housing affordability described as 'absurdly unaffordable'
Iron ore prices under pressure ('iron ore roaches seethe'); Japan diverting Australian LNG to its own market while East Coast gas supply tightens
Mining exploration positives: Critica rare earths (58% carbonate), Augustus 30g/t gold target, Dalaroo copper-nickel-PGE, Aurum Côte d'Ivoire gold
Qantas ground staff strike looms over 'Joyce-era' bargaining; Coles maintains elevated milk prices; fashion brands Cue and Veronika Maine face collapse
Anthropic confirmed $31bn data centre in western Queensland, a structural boost to WA/QLD infrastructure and tech capex

sectors.trend: Iron ore under pressure with China demand concerns; however, exploration upside in gold (Augustus, Aurum), copper-nickel-PGE (Dalaroo), and rare earths (Critica) provides offsetting catalysts. Coal policy uncertainty (Albo government) weighs on FMG.AX, WDS.AX.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX and RIO.AX face near-term iron ore headwinds; junior explorers (AUG.AX, DLR.AX, CRI.AX) offer asymmetric upside. Gold miners benefit from safe-haven flows amid Middle East risk.

sectors.trend: Big four banks advanced on the session as bond yields eased. RBA's 'sensible level' warning and IMF fiscal caution suggest rates stay elevated, supporting NIMs but pressuring credit growth and state borrowing costs.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX benefit from sustained higher-for-longer rates. State government debt servicing (headline 56) could pressure sovereign-linked credit. ACCC real estate monopoly probe (59) is a tailwind for mortgage lenders.

sectors.trend: Houthi attacks on Saudi oil and petrol price shock (33) lift crude and fuel costs. Japan diverting Australian LNG (30) tightens East Coast gas supply. Victoria backing away from renewable transmission (31) delays clean-energy capex.
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, WEL.AX, SXG.AX benefit from higher oil/gas prices. Coal producers face policy risk. REITs and utilities face input-cost inflation. LNG exporters (BHP.AX, WDS.AX) see pricing support.

sectors.trend: Coles maintains elevated milk prices (44); Qantas strike risk (41); fashion brands Cue/Veronika Maine near collapse (72). Housing unaffordability (34) and tenant relief (53) signal a bifurcated consumer landscape.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WOW.AX face margin pressure from input costs. QAN.AX exposed to industrial action. Consumer discretionary names under pressure; staples (WES.AX) offer relative defensiveness.

sectors.trend: Anthropic's $31bn QLD data centre (71) is a landmark capex event. AI investment race continues globally (63, 67). Anthropic also active in WA (17).
sectors.implications: Structural tailwind for QLD/WA construction, power, and telecoms. ASX-listed data centre and infrastructure plays (e.g., VMC.AX, IAG.AX) benefit. Global AI capex supports sentiment.

sectors.trend: No major ASX healthcare headlines today; flu season awareness (6) is a minor seasonal note. CSL.AX remains a core defensive holding.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, SGH.AX, OSH.AX continue to offer portfolio diversification in a volatile rate environment.

Middle East oil shock: Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure threaten global supply and lift AUD-linked commodity prices
Japan rate hike: pressures AUD/USD, widens yield differentials, complicates RBA's inflation fight
Commodity bifurcation: iron ore weak, gold/rare earths/copper exploration strong, LNG pricing supported
Housing affordability crisis: 'absurdly unaffordable' (34), tenant relief (53), ACCC real estate probe (59)

Industrial action: Qantas strike (41), Queensland Rail resolved (3) – mixed labour risk
Structural tech capex: Anthropic $31bn QLD data centre reshapes infrastructure landscape

Hold energy exposure (WDS.AX, WEL.AX); monitor Brent crude; consider AUD hedge given commodity-linked currency
Maintain defensive allocation (CSL.AX, WES.AX); reduce leverage; monitor unemployment and retail sales data

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to consolidate in a range. RBA rate decision and Middle East oil developments are the dominant near-term catalysts. Banks and energy outperform; REITs and consumer discretionary lag. AUD/USD volatile on Japan rate hike and oil flows. Expect 1–2% index volatility into the RBA meeting.
market_outlook.long_term: 6–12 month outlook is cautiously constructive but constrained. Higher-for-longer rates and 2027 recession risk cap multiple expansion. Structural positives: Anthropic data centre capex, rare earths/gold exploration pipeline, LNG pricing support. Key risk: if Middle East oil shock escalates, inflation re-acceleration could force another RBA hike, triggering a sharper correction.
